name: – Michalis Hadjipantela – Commission proposal to the Council
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Council regulation amending Regulation (EU) No 904/2010 as regards the access of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) and the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) to value added tax information at Union level
part_text:
The European Parliament wants two European bodies that fight fraud — the European Public Prosecutor's Office and the European Anti-Fraud Office — to get direct, centralised access to national VAT data. Today they cannot easily see this information. Parliament also wants customs data on imports shared automatically when it suggests VAT fraud, and safeguards so access stays tied to specific investigations. It asks the Commission to propose common minimum penalties for the most serious VAT and customs fraud.

- **What changes:** The two fraud bodies get direct access to VAT and customs data, with strict limits.
- **Who it affects:** National tax and customs authorities, importers, and the two European fraud bodies.
- **What happens next:** The Council decides; Parliament must be consulted again if the text changes substantially.
